propositions: On the agentic execution path, accumulated tool-result message history is re-sent uncached every turn, causing input cost to grow quadratically (O(N^2)) in the number of turns.

cache_settings_for() sets only two of four available cache breakpoints (anthropic_cache_instructions and anthropic_cache_tool_definitions) but does not set anthropic_cache or bedrock_cache_messages, leaving the message tail unwritten to cache.

The system-only cache breakpoint causes the telemetry predicate warn_if_cache_ineffective to never fire because cache_read_tokens is always nonzero from the system block, masking the quadratic uncached input cost from visibility.

For agentic multi-turn workloads, the Anthropic and Bedrock arms require different cache keys (anthropic_cache vs bedrock_cache_messages respectively) due to provider asymmetry; Bedrock rejects a top-level cache_control key.
Single-turn execution paths must remain byte-identical to avoid regression, since they do not benefit from multi-turn message-tail caching.
